newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to protest to U.N. over PLO land law.
newsitem.headline: Israel to protest to U.N. over PLO land law.

text.p: Israel said on Wednesday it would complain to the U.N. committee on human rights over the Palestinian Authority's decision to impose the death penalty on people who sell land to Israelis.

"The cabinet secretary, who is also the chairman of the government forum following anti-Semitism worldwide, is about to present the U.N. committee on human rights with a complaint about the Palestinian Authority decision," a statement issued by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said.
"The decision is in essence racist and reeks of anti- Semitism."

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said in an interview published on Wednesday he backed the recent Palestinian Authority decision to enforce an old Jordanian law in the West Bank imposing the death penalty for land sales to Jews.
"We are talking about isolated traitors," Arafat said. "And we will impose against them what is on the law books. That is our right and our obligation to protect our land."
Israel has linked the ban on land sales with the recent killings of two Palestinian land dealers found dead in the West Bank. The Authority has denied any involvement in the killings.
The Palestinians hope to establish a state in the West Bank and Gaza Strip with East Jerusalem as its capital.

More than 130,000 Israelis have settled amid some two million Palestinians in the areas, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war. The Authority hopes to stop settlement expansion with the stiff land law.
